preconditions.description: T is the number of test cases, an integer between 1 and 2013 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(S, str) and 1 <= len(S) <= 2013 and all(c in 'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ?' for c in S) for S in test_cases)
preconditions.description: Each test case string S has length between 1 and 2013, and consists only of uppercase letters A-Z or '?'.

postconditions.expression: all(len(result) == len(S) for S, result in zip(test_cases, outputs))
postconditions.description: The output string has the same length as the input string.

postconditions.expression: all(all(c in 'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ' for c in result) for result in outputs)
postconditions.description: The output string contains only uppercase letters A-Z (no '?' remains).

postconditions.expression: all(all(c == S[i] or c == '?' for i, c in enumerate(result)) for S, result in zip(test_cases, outputs))
postconditions.description: The output string matches the input string where the input is not '?' (unchanged letters).

postconditions.expression: all(count_chef_substrings(result) >= count_chef_substrings(alternative) for S, result in zip(test_cases, outputs) for alternative in possible_replacements(S))
postconditions.description: The output string maximizes the number of 'CHEF' substrings among all possible replacements of '?' in the input string.

postconditions.expression: all(result == lex_smallest_among_max_chef(S, outputs) for S, result in zip(test_cases, outputs))
postconditions.description: Among all strings with the maximum number of 'CHEF' substrings, the output is the lexicographically smallest one.
